name: Willie Dixon
note: Two of his songs, You Shook Me and I Can't Quit You Baby, are on the first album, and he is now credited as a co-writer of Whole Lotta Love.

name: Howlin' Wolf
note: In 1969 the band played his Killing Floor on stage, and it grew into The Lemon Song on Led Zeppelin II. Later releases credit him as Chester Burnett.

name: Muddy Waters
note: His 1962 recording of Willie Dixon's You Need Love is the song behind Whole Lotta Love.

name: Memphis Minnie & Kansas Joe McCoy
note: Their 1929 record When the Levee Breaks, about the Mississippi flood of 1927, became the last track on Led Zeppelin IV.

name: Bert Jansch
note: Page learned from the Scottish folk guitarist's arrangement of the traditional Blackwaterside, which became Black Mountain Side on the first album.

name: Davy Graham
note: His open-tuned guitar version of She Moved Through the Fair is the model for White Summer, Page's solo piece in the band's early sets.

name: Elvis Presley
note: An early influence on Plant as a singer. Plant met him after seeing him play the LA Forum in May 1974.

name: Umm Kulthum
note: Plant heard the Egyptian singer in Marrakech in 1970 and said her voice drove him "to distraction". He has said he followed the orchestration of her Cairo orchestra for years.

name: Gene Krupa
note: The swing drummer was an important early influence on John Bonham, who talks about him in the 2025 documentary Becoming Led Zeppelin.

name: Rush
note: Geddy Lee has said the first Led Zeppelin album helped shape Rush's earliest sound, and their first records were often compared with the band.

name: Heart
note: Ann and Nancy Wilson played Stairway to Heaven in front of Page, Plant and Jones at the 2012 Kennedy Center Honors, with Jason Bonham on drums.

name: Beastie Boys
note: Rhymin & Stealin, the opening track of Licensed to Ill (1986), is built on Bonham's drums from When the Levee Breaks, one of the most sampled beats in hip hop.

name: Puff Daddy
note: Come with Me, from the 1998 Godzilla soundtrack, is built on Kashmir, with Jimmy Page playing guitar on it.

name: Dave Grohl
note: Has called Bonham the greatest rock drummer of all time, and later formed Them Crooked Vultures with John Paul Jones.

name: Soundgarden
note: Often compared with Zeppelin in their early years. In 2014 Chris Cornell interviewed Page on stage in Los Angeles about the band's history.

name: Jack White
note: Shared the screen with Page and The Edge in the 2008 guitar documentary It Might Get Loud.

name: Greta Van Fleet
note: The Michigan band drew constant comparison with Zeppelin; Plant said of them, "They are Led Zeppelin I".
